parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text:
Reaction 1 is an oxidation reaction.

Give the reagent(s) and conditions required for reaction 1.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
Construct an equation to represent reaction 1.

Use [O] to represent an oxygen atom from the oxidising agent in this reaction.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: Suggest the type of reaction that occurs in reaction 2.

parts.label: (a)(iv)
parts.text:
$\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ acts as a homogeneous catalyst in reaction 3.

Explain why $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is described as homogeneous.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Reaction 2 needs to take place in the absence of water to prevent formation of compound **C**.

{{figure:pdf_visual_03.png}}

If **C** is present in the reaction mixture of reaction 3, a different compound, compound **D**, will also form. Compound **D** has two identical functional groups.

The infrared spectrum of **D** shows strong absorptions at $1100\text{ cm}^{-1}$ and $1720\text{ cm}^{-1}$, but no absorption due to O-H bonds.

Use the Data Booklet to identify the functional group present in **D**.

Explain your answer as fully as you can.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Suggest why $\text{NaBH}_4$ is not a suitable reagent to make **F**, $\text{(CH}_2\text{OH)}_2$, from **C**. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Construct an equation for the reaction of $\text{(CH}_2\text{OH)}_2$ with $\text{SOCl}_2$ to form **G**, $\text{(CH}_2\text{Cl)}_2$.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Explain why **C** is very soluble in water.
